title: Federal Revenue Service Public Exam Advances with Terms of Reference Revision
seoTitle: Federal Revenue Service Exam: Terms of Reference Revised
subtitle: Understand the changes in the organizing body selection process and the foreseen timeline
excerpt: The Federal Revenue Service revised the terms of reference guiding the hiring of the organizing body for the 146-vacancy public exam, maintaining its scope and moving.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: Blog Gran Cursos Online, Estratégia Concursos, Qconcursos Folha Dirigida
contentHtml:
The Federal Revenue Service has updated the Terms of Reference governing the selection of the institution responsible for organizing the Tax and Customs Career public exam, maintaining the object and scope of services.

Terms of Reference Revision

The document was refined based on issues raised during the market research phase, aiming for greater clarity and precision in technical and operational aspects. The revision does not alter the object or scope of the contract but allows for specific adjustments by those who have already submitted a commercial proposal within the original deadline.

Exam Timeline and Stages

The public exam, authorized in July 2026 by MGI Ordinance No. 5,505, provides for 146 vacancies – 116 for Tax Analyst and 30 for Tax Auditor. The market survey phase began in September, with the expectation of hiring the organizing body in October and publishing the official notice in December 2026. The tests will be divided into two stages, with the second being a mandatory professional training course, eliminatory in nature.

Deadline for Organizing Body Proposals

The Federal Revenue Service extended the deadline for interested institutions to submit commercial proposals until September 25. This extension is part of the market survey that precedes the definition of the organizing body.

Impact of Organizing Body Choice on Preparation

While the organizing body is yet to be defined, candidates can study the history of previous organizers such as FGV, Cesgranrio, and Cebraspe. Each has a distinct examination model – multiple-choice questions with extensive statements (FGV), direct alternatives (Cesgranrio), and True or False format (Cebraspe). Understanding these profiles helps candidates adapt their training before the official notice is published.

Mock Exams and Study Resources

For those already preparing, Estratégia Concursos offers the 2nd Special Federal Revenue Service Mock Exam for Tax Auditor, featuring 140 multiple-choice questions and a discursive test, focused on the FGV organizing body style. Live correction takes place after the answer key is released, allowing candidates to evaluate their performance before the official notice.
